test: paired DeLong (DeLong 1988; Sun & Xu 2014 fast algorithm), midranks for ties
implementation: src/covid_mortality/evaluation/delong.py (numpy only, shared with Task A)
pairing: the same Test patients for every model; predictions are merged on subject_id and the row order is verified before testing. Two-sample AUC comparisons are not used.

A.question: does multimodal Late Fusion improve on each clinical tabular model

B.question: does multimodal Late Fusion improve on the two single-modality reference models (the clinical reference and the imaging model)

multiplicity_correction: Holm, applied separately within each family
note_on_overlap: `late_fusion vs clinical_lr` belongs to both families, so it carries two Holm-adjusted p-values, one per family. Report the family alongside every adjusted p-value so the two are not confused; the unadjusted p-value is the same in both.

comparisons.interpretation: Late Fusion (Task C primary) minus Clinical LR = -0.0016 (95% CI -0.0122 to +0.0091); Holm-adjusted p = 0.7697 within family A. The difference is not statistically significant after Holm correction. This is not evidence of equivalence: with 17 events the confidence interval is wide and includes differences that would matter clinically.

Late Fusion (Task C primary) minus Clinical XGBoost = +0.0159 (95% CI -0.0099 to +0.0417); Holm-adjusted p = 0.5398 within family A. The difference is not statistically significant after Holm correction. This is not evidence of equivalence: with 17 events the confidence interval is wide and includes differences that would matter clinically.

Late Fusion (Task C primary) minus Clinical MLP = +0.0207 (95% CI -0.0095 to +0.0509); Holm-adjusted p = 0.5398 within family A. The difference is not statistically significant after Holm correction. This is not evidence of equivalence: with 17 events the confidence interval is wide and includes differences that would matter clinically.

Late Fusion (Task C primary) minus Clinical LR = -0.0016 (95% CI -0.0122 to +0.0091); Holm-adjusted p = 0.7697 within family B. The difference is not statistically significant after Holm correction. This is not evidence of equivalence: with 17 events the confidence interval is wide and includes differences that would matter clinically.

Late Fusion (Task C primary) minus CXR ResNet18 = +0.1102 (95% CI +0.0401 to +0.1804); Holm-adjusted p = 0.0042 within family B. The difference is statistically significant at the 0.05 level after Holm correction.

caution: A lack of statistical significance must not be interpreted as equivalence. With 128 Test patients and 17 deaths these comparisons have limited power.
